main.title: Shadow of the Beast
main.subtitle: Aarbron's journey returns in a new form
main.summary: Shadow of the Beast is Heavy Spectrum's PlayStation 4 reimagining of the 1989 game, released on 17 May 2016. Aarbron, transformed into a monstrous servant, moves through an alien world shaped by the power that corrupted him. Side-on exploration connects platforming, puzzles and close combat, while three-dimensional scenery preserves the layered landscapes associated with the original. The remake develops its own fighting system rather than reproducing every earlier interaction. The player reads the enemies gathering around Aarbron and chooses how to break their formation before another attack closes the available space.

cards.heading: Aarbron's journey returns in a new form
cards.text: Shadow of the Beast is Heavy Spectrum's PlayStation 4 reimagining of the 1989 game, released on 17 May 2016. Aarbron, transformed into a monstrous servant, moves through an alien world shaped by the power that corrupted him. Side-on exploration connects platforming, puzzles and close combat, while three-dimensional scenery preserves the layered landscapes associated with the original. The remake develops its own fighting system rather than reproducing every earlier interaction. The player reads the enemies gathering around Aarbron and chooses how to break their formation before another attack closes the available space.

cards.heading: The enemy's protection determines the response
cards.text: Counterattacks and combinations give the player ways to deal with approaching opponents, while shield-bearing enemies require a change of position before they can be struck effectively. Traps and environmental puzzles interrupt the fighting with other uses for movement and observation. The health bar makes repeated mistakes consequential, encouraging a more deliberate reading of each group. Success depends on selecting the appropriate response rather than repeating one attack against every target. That emphasis gives Aarbron's physical strength a controlled rhythm, as the player alternates between recognising an opening and exploiting it.

cards.heading: A new game keeps the earlier landscape nearby
cards.text: Ian Livingstone composed the score, and the original Shadow of the Beast is included as an unlockable extra, with an optional infinite-lives mode making it easier to explore. This places the new interpretation beside the work that inspired it without requiring the two to use identical systems. The remake's detailed landscapes recall the importance of visual atmosphere to the Amiga release, while the expanded combat establishes a different playable structure. It is a return built around the memory of a striking world, giving that world a new action game for another console generation.

main.title: Overwatch
main.subtitle: A Team Readable at a Glance
main.summary: Overwatch is Blizzard?s 2016 team shooter, where distinct heroes combine abilities and can switch roles during a match.

cards.heading: Heroes with distinct roles
cards.text: Overwatch is Blizzard?s 2016 team shooter, released on May 24 for PC, PlayStation 4 and Xbox One. Heroes have distinct weapons, abilities and roles, including protection, healing and rapid movement. Players can change hero during a match to adjust their team?s response.

cards.heading: Recognising a hero in battle
cards.text: Body shape, posture, weapons and sound make heroes recognisable in a busy fight. Seeing Reinhardt, Tracer or Mercy gives opponents and teammates information about their likely abilities. The character designs support quick identification as effects fill the screen.

cards.heading: Changing the team?s approach
cards.text: Switching heroes lets a team reconsider its composition. A group struggling with one approach can seek more protection, mobility, ranged attacks or healing. Players must understand what the team needs as well as their own character?s abilities.

cards.heading: Maps built around shared objectives
cards.text: Payloads, control points and capture zones give teams shared objectives. Choke points, high ground and side routes matter differently to mobile characters, tanks and long-range fighters. Cooperation helps turn those positions into an advantage.

main.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Blood and Wine
main.subtitle: One last toast in Toussaint
main.summary: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Blood and Wine (Polish: Wiedźmin 3: Dziki Gon – Krew i wino) is the second expansion pack for the 2015 video game The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, following the first expansion, Hearts of Stone.

cards.heading: A duchy untouched by war
cards.text: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Blood and Wine (Polish: Wiedźmin 3: Dziki Gon – Krew i wino) is the second expansion pack for the 2015 video game The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, following the first expansion, Hearts of Stone. Developed by CD Projekt Red, the expansion follows Geralt of Rivia as he travels to Toussaint, a duchy untouched by the war taking place in the base game, as he hopes to track down a mysterious beast terrorizing the region.

cards.heading: The expansion launches to acclaim
cards.text: Blood and Wine was released for PlayStation 4, Windows, and Xbox One on 31 May 2016, and later released for the Nintendo Switch on 15 October 2019, with PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S versions released on 14 December 2022. The expansion received widespread acclaim from critics, winning a number of awards. Many consider it to be one of the best downloadable content packs of all time.

main.title: Mirror's Edge Catalyst
main.subtitle: Faith runs through the city of Glass
main.summary: On June 7, 2016 DICE brought Faith back in the city of Glass and expanded first-person parkour inside a more open structure.

cards.heading: Faith returns to Glass
cards.text: Mirror?s Edge Catalyst is DICE?s 2016 first-person action adventure, released on June 7. Faith returns in the city of Glass, with parkour routes through a more open environment. Colour, architecture and animation help players recognise where to run, jump and change height.

cards.heading: Movement becomes a means of defence
cards.text: Combat mechanics of the game received an overhaul and a new combat system was developed as traversal is greatly emphasised in the game. Also, though only used sparingly in the previous game, Mirror's Edge Catalyst has removed the use of guns by the player altogether, focusing on Faith's running and parkour movements and quick melee-style attacks to take down or evade her enemies. Faith enters focus mode while she is running, and with sufficient focus Faith can evade bullets from enemies. According to Sara Jansson, the senior producer of the game, the combat and fighting featured is an extension to the game's movement instead of a separated set. When Faith is performing a finishing move, the game switches to a third-person perspective.

cards.heading: Runner Vision and routes through Glass
cards.text: Faith moves through the city of Glass in first person, linking ledges, rooftops and ziplines into routes. The open city replaces the original's separate linear levels, allowing different approaches to a destination. Marking an objective activates Runner Vision, highlighting useful scenery in red. A MAG Rope helps bridge buildings, while the Disruptor disables equipment such as fans or security cameras. Time trials, races and environmental puzzles ask the player to return to those routes with another purpose. Collectible GridLeaks provide smaller diversions during travel, keeping the city useful beyond the immediate campaign objective.

cards.heading: Runners outside the city?s network
cards.text: So-called Runners, freelance messengers skilled at parkour, refuse to be connected to the Grid and live on rooftops, making their living from covert delivery jobs while evading corporate security. The game centers around a Runner named Faith, and her efforts to help other Runners overthrow the corporate government and stop Reflection.

main.title: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney – Spirit of Justice
main.subtitle: A courtroom governed by the dead
main.summary: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney – Spirit of Justice is Capcom's Nintendo 3DS legal adventure dividing its cases between the Wright Anything Agency and the kingdom of Khura'in. Phoenix travels to meet Maya Fey and encounters a justice system that relies on a victim's final experiences. Apollo and Athena continue the agency's work elsewhere, connecting the two settings through a returning defence team. The unfamiliar courtroom gives Phoenix a different kind of testimony to challenge, while the wider story follows the consequences of trying to defend someone within that system.

cards.heading: A courtroom governed by the dead
cards.text: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney – Spirit of Justice is Capcom's Nintendo 3DS legal adventure dividing its cases between the Wright Anything Agency and the kingdom of Khura'in. Phoenix travels to meet Maya Fey and encounters a justice system that relies on a victim's final experiences. Apollo and Athena continue the agency's work elsewhere, connecting the two settings through a returning defence team. The unfamiliar courtroom gives Phoenix a different kind of testimony to challenge, while the wider story follows the consequences of trying to defend someone within that system.

cards.heading: A vision still needs an interpretation
cards.text: Khura'in's Divination Séance presents the victim's last sensations as a vision accompanied by the priestess's explanation. The player examines what is seen and perceived, then identifies where that material contradicts the interpretation offered to the court. A supernatural source therefore becomes something that still needs careful reading. The sequence adds another form of evidence to the series' hearings. An apparently decisive account can contain a misleading assumption, and the defence makes progress by separating the experience itself from what somebody claims it proves about the crime.

cards.heading: Three lawyers bring different methods
cards.text: Outside the Khura'in hearings, the returning lawyers retain their distinctive investigative techniques. Phoenix can confront hidden secrets through Psyche-Locks, Apollo notices revealing habits, and Athena examines conflicting emotions with the Mood Matrix. Investigations also allow three-dimensional scenes to be viewed from different perspectives while gathering evidence. These tools create different ways of approaching a reluctant witness or an incomplete account. The cases continue to depend on the same basic work of understanding the record, but the available methods change with the lawyer and the place in which the hearing unfolds.

main.title: INSIDE
main.subtitle: A boy crosses a hostile industrial world
main.summary: On June 29, 2016 Playdead released INSIDE worldwide on Xbox One.

cards.heading: A boy in a hostile world
cards.text: INSIDE is Playdead?s 2016 puzzle-platform adventure, first released for Xbox One on June 29. An unnamed boy runs, hides and solves puzzles through a hostile industrial landscape. Light, animation, sound and the arrangement of objects guide players with little explicit instruction.

cards.heading: Danger, death and checkpoints
cards.text: The player can die in a multitude of ways, including drowning, being shot with a gun or tranquilizer dart, mauled by dogs, ensnared by security machines, being blown apart by shockwaves, and others. As in the predecessor game Limbo, these deaths are presented realistically and are often graphic, but to a larger degree, earning the ESRB's Mature rating as opposed to Limbo's Teen rating. If the character dies, the game continues from the most recent checkpoint.

cards.heading: Exploring and controlling bodies
cards.text: Inside is a puzzle platformer. The player character is an unnamed boy or young man who explores a surreal and mostly monochromatic environment presented as a 2.5D platform game. The game is dark, with color used sparingly to highlight both the player and certain parts of the environment. The game is mostly silent, with the exception of occasional musical cues, the boy's vocals, dogs barking, equipment and sound effects. The character can walk, run, swim, climb, and use objects to overcome obstacles and progress in the game. At select areas of the game, the character can use a device (similar in appearance to the later-mentioned glowing orbs) to control bodies in order to complete certain puzzles, a mechanic that IGN's Marty Sliva compared to a similar one in The Swapper. At various points in the game, the player may discover hidden rooms containing glowing orbs. If all the orbs are deactivated during a playthrough, the player unlocks the game's alternate ending.

cards.heading: Sound and animation respond together
cards.text: Inside has a close integration of the game-play and audio, with some puzzles set directly to visual-aural cues. This required Andersen to work more closely with the game-play developers than he had in Limbo. This enabled additional visual elements tied to the audio; Andersen noted that the boy's chest movements related to breathing are tied to the sound effects he created for his breathing, which themselves are influenced by where the character is in the game, with differences being calm and panicked emotions depending on location. Andersen collaborated with the design team on the game's general structure and pacing to provide scenes where the music builds up atmospheric tension.

main.title: Pokémon GO
main.subtitle: The map becomes a meeting place
main.summary: A smartphone game connected a familiar collection to streets, parks and routines.

cards.heading: The map becomes part of play
cards.text: Pokémon GO brought catching and collecting into a location-based mobile game, first released on July 6, 2016 in Australia, New Zealand and the United States before reaching other countries. Walking through the physical world changed what could appear on the screen, linking play to places players already used or newly discovered.

cards.heading: Access depends on the real world
cards.text: Its gatherings also made questions of access visible: not every neighbourhood has equal places to play, and not every player can move in the same way. Location-aware design ties virtual systems to the opportunities and limits of real environments.

cards.heading: The world becomes a map
cards.text: Players can customize their avatars after creating an account, with the option of keeping the default avatar. Avatars are displayed on the game map according to the player's GPS location. The map features "PokéStops" and "Gyms"; players can equip PokéStops with "Lure Modules" to attract wild Pokémon, including potentially rare ones. Gyms serve as battle arenas for team-based king-of- the-hill matches. These locations are typically at points of interest and originally adapted from Ingress portals. Some Gyms and PokéStops have been placed in problematic locations, such as the Korean Demilitarized Zone and the abandoned Bagram Air Force Base. Since 2019, player submissions have also been included in these locations, subject to review by other players.

cards.heading: Pokémon in your surroundings
cards.text: Players' avatars move across the game map to reflect their real-world location as they explore their surroundings. Different Pokémon species appear in various regions worldwide, with Water-type Pokémon typically found near bodies of water. When players encounter a Pokémon, they can view it against a live-rendered background or in augmented reality (AR) mode. AR mode uses the camera and gyroscope on the player's mobile device to display a Pokémon as if it were present in the real world. Players can capture screenshots, called "Snapshots", of the Pokémon they encounter, regardless of whether the AR feature is enabled.

cards.heading: The act of catching
cards.text: In Pokémon Go, players do not battle wild Pokémon to capture them. Instead, they throw a Poké Ball toward the Pokémon by flicking it upward on the screen. Factors affecting the success rate include the Pokémon's catch rate, timing, and the type of Poké Ball used. After capturing a Pokémon, players receive Candy and Stardust as rewards. Candy is used for leveling up or to evolve Pokémon, while Stardust is used to increase a Pokémon's Combat Power (CP). Each Pokémon evolution line has its own type of Candy. The maximum player level was initially 40 but was raised to 50 on November 30, 2020. It was subsequently increased to level 80 following a leveling update on October 15, 2025. Players can transfer Pokémon to get more Candy and free up space in their collection. Shiny Pokémon can be found through various methods, such as chance encounters or special events like "Community Day". Many players aim to complete the Pokédex by catching and evolving all Pokémon.

main.title: Yo-kai Watch 3
main.subtitle: Two towns share a supernatural problem
main.summary: Yo-kai Watch 3 is Level-5's Nintendo 3DS role-playing adventure following two protagonists in connected settings. Nate moves to the American-inspired town of BBQ, while Hailey Anne Thomas becomes involved with a detective agency in Springdale. Their separate journeys introduce another population of Yo-kai and gradually connect their discoveries. Japan first received Sushi and Tempura versions, followed by the expanded Sukiyaki edition on which the later international release was based. The change of place gives the series' everyday supernatural comedy another community and another young investigator to follow.

cards.heading: Two towns share a supernatural problem
cards.text: Yo-kai Watch 3 is Level-5's Nintendo 3DS role-playing adventure following two protagonists in connected settings. Nate moves to the American-inspired town of BBQ, while Hailey Anne Thomas becomes involved with a detective agency in Springdale. Their separate journeys introduce another population of Yo-kai and gradually connect their discoveries. Japan first received Sushi and Tempura versions, followed by the expanded Sukiyaki edition on which the later international release was based. The change of place gives the series' everyday supernatural comedy another community and another young investigator to follow.

cards.heading: A board replaces the medal wheel
cards.text: Combat replaces the earlier rotating medal arrangement with the Tactics Board, allowing active Yo-kai to be moved around a grid. Their position becomes a practical concern during the fight, changing how the team responds to incoming attacks and makes use of the available space. The player continues to intervene while companions perform their ordinary actions automatically. This reworking gives the sequel a different physical rhythm on the touchscreen. Preparing a capable collection remains important, but positioning the current group adds another immediate decision within an encounter.

cards.heading: Another perspective on Springdale
cards.text: Moving between Nate's life in BBQ and Hailey Anne's investigations gives the adventure two different routes into its mysteries. A new town supplies unfamiliar places and creatures, while returning to Springdale allows a different protagonist to encounter the established setting. The expanded international version gathers material from the Japanese releases into one journey. Its larger structure makes collecting and meeting Yo-kai part of two stories at once, using the contrast between familiar surroundings and a new home to keep the hidden world open to discovery.

main.title: No Man's Sky
main.subtitle: An expanding universe, a second beginning
main.summary: No Man's Sky is an action-adventure survival game developed and published by Hello Games.

cards.heading: A procedurally generated universe
cards.text: The game is built around four pillars: exploration, survival, combat, and trading. Players can engage with the entirety of a procedurally generated deterministic open world universe, which includes over 18 quintillion planets. Through the game's procedural generation system, planets have their own ecosystems with unique forms of flora and fauna, and various alien species may engage the player in combat or trade within planetary systems. Players advance by mining resources to power and improve their equipment, buying and selling resources using currencies earned by documenting flora and fauna or trading with the lifeforms, building planetary bases and expanding space fleets, or otherwise following the game's overarching plot by seeking out the mystery around the entity known as The Atlas.

cards.heading: The Traveller and the starship
cards.text: The Traveller begins beside a damaged spacecraft on an unfamiliar planet. A multitool scans, mines and collects materials, while the survival suit and jetpack provide ways to cross the terrain. Repairing and fuelling the ship opens journeys between planets and eventually other star systems. Exploration, trade and combat all depend on maintaining and improving that equipment. The player may follow the Atlas towards the galactic centre or pursue other interests. A distant destination therefore begins with immediate decisions about what to gather and which part of the ship must work before departure.

cards.heading: Science fiction and a small studio
cards.text: Sean Murray, the founder of Hello Games, wanted to create a game that captured the sense of exploration and optimism of science fiction literature and art of the 1970s and 1980s. The game was developed over three years by a small team at Hello Games with promotional and publishing help from Sony Interactive Entertainment. The gaming media saw this as an ambitious project for a small team, and Murray and Hello Games drew significant attention leading to its release.

cards.heading: The difficult launch
cards.text: No Man's Sky initially received mixed reviews at its 2016 launch, with some critics praising the technical achievements of the procedurally generated universe, while others considered the gameplay lackluster and repetitive. However, the critical response was marred by the lack of several features that had been reported to be featured, particularly multiplayer capabilities. The game was further criticised due to Hello Games's lack of communication in the months following the launch, creating backlash from some of its players. Murray later stated that Hello Games had failed to control the hype and the larger-than-expected player count at launch, and have taken an approach of remaining quiet about updates until they are nearly ready to release. The promotion and marketing for No Man's Sky became a subject of debate and has been cited as an example of what to avoid in video game marketing.

cards.heading: Years of free expansions
cards.text: Since the game's initial release, Hello Games has continued to improve and expand No Man's Sky to achieve the vision of the experience they wanted to build. The game has received multiple free major content updates that have added several previously missing features, such as multiplayer components, while adding features like surface vehicles, base-building, space fleet management, cross-platform play, and virtual reality support. This has substantially improved No Man's Sky's overall reception, with multiple websites citing it as one of the greatest redemption stories in the gaming industry.

main.title: Bound
main.subtitle: A dancer inside a memory
main.summary: Bound is Plastic's PlayStation 4 platform game, released on 16 August 2016. A princess moves through a shifting geometric world while the surrounding story follows a woman revisiting her childhood memories. The princess's movement draws on ballet, making each step, jump and defensive action part of a continuous performance. Abstract structures replace familiar landscapes, breaking apart and reforming as the journey continues. The personal events behind them are gradually revealed, giving the unusual scenery a connection to a life beyond the visible fantasy.

cards.heading: A dancer inside a memory
cards.text: Bound is Plastic's PlayStation 4 platform game, released on 16 August 2016. A princess moves through a shifting geometric world while the surrounding story follows a woman revisiting her childhood memories. The princess's movement draws on ballet, making each step, jump and defensive action part of a continuous performance. Abstract structures replace familiar landscapes, breaking apart and reforming as the journey continues. The personal events behind them are gradually revealed, giving the unusual scenery a connection to a life beyond the visible fantasy.

cards.heading: Let the movement carry attention
cards.text: The dancer runs, balances and crosses gaps with gestures that retain the character of a performed routine. Dancing can repel threats, so an action used for protection also reinforces the way she occupies the space. Edge protection on certain platforms reduces accidental falls, allowing more attention to remain on the figure and changing environment. Some sections still carry a risk of falling, with a nearby return keeping the journey moving. The design gives the performance room to be watched rather than requiring every step to become a demanding platform challenge.

cards.heading: An abstract place with a human source
cards.text: Scenes outside the princess's world connect its Queen, monster and collapsing structures to the woman's past. The player can recognise those relationships as the journey unfolds, reading the fantasy through the memories that surround it. Oleg Shpudeiko's music accompanies the movement and changing architecture. Critics praised Bound's visual identity and originality, while some found the interactions too limited. That balance defines the experience: its route is built to reveal a personal story through the dancer's body, the forms around her and the spaces that gradually disappear.
